verses.1: Having heard that speech of Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemies (Rama) said, "O one of good vows, narrate the slaying of Vritra completely."
verses.2: Thus addressed by Rama, the enhancer of Sumitra's joy, who was of good vows, again narrated the divine story.
verses.3: Having heard the words of Indra and all the gods, Vishnu spoke these words to all the gods, with Indra at their forefront.
verses.4: I am indeed bound by a prior friendship with the great Vritra, and therefore I cannot kill this great demon for your benefit.
verses.5: Your supreme happiness must certainly be achieved, therefore I shall explain a method by which Vritra can be killed.
verses.6: O best of gods, I shall indeed divide myself into three parts, and thereby Indra will kill Vritra without a doubt.
verses.7: Let one part of me go into Indra, the second into his thunderbolt, and the third into the earth; then Indra will be able to kill Vritra.
verses.8: When the Lord of Gods (Vishnu) spoke thus, the gods then replied, "O slayer of demons, what you say is indeed true, there is no doubt about it."
verses.9: "May good fortune be with you; we shall now go, eager to slay Vritrasura, and O most generous one, you should empower Indra with your own might."
verses.10: Then all the great-souled gods, led by Indra, proceeded towards that forest where the mighty demon Vritra resided.
verses.11: They saw the foremost of demons, Vritra, endowed with immense splendor and radiating heat, as if he were drinking up the three worlds and burning the very sky.
verses.12: And having seen that foremost of demons, the gods were struck with fear, wondering, "How shall we kill him? How can we avoid defeat?"
verses.13: While the gods were contemplating there, the thousand-eyed Indra, the destroyer of cities, grasped the thunderbolt with both hands and hurled it onto Vritra's head.
verses.14: As Vritra's head fell, burning like the terrible, great-flamed fire of universal destruction, the world experienced immense terror.
verses.15: The greatly renowned lord of gods, contemplating the inconceivable slaying of Vritra, quickly went to a secluded corner of the world.
verses.16: As that Indra was going, the sin of Brahmanicide quickly followed him and fell upon his limbs, enveloping him in sorrow.
verses.17: The gods, whose enemies were slain but whose Indra had disappeared, with Agni as their leader, repeatedly worshipped Vishnu, the lord of the three worlds.
verses.18: O Supreme Lord, you are the ultimate refuge, the primeval father of the world, who has assumed the form of Vishnu for the protection of all beings.
verses.19: O best among gods, Vritra has been killed by you, and now the sin of Brahmanicide afflicts Indra; please prescribe a means of liberation for him from this sin.
verses.20: Having heard the words of the gods, Vishnu said, "Let Indra worship me alone, and I shall purify the wielder of the thunderbolt."
verses.21: Having worshipped me with a meritorious Ashvamedha sacrifice, Indra will again attain his fearless sovereignty over the gods.
verses.22: Having thus delivered that nectar-like message to the gods, Vishnu, the lord of gods, returned to heaven, being praised by them. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 85 ।। Thus ends the eighty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
